title: Muraja'ah: the Juz' 'Amma rota and 'Abasa 1 to 16: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y7 lesson 15 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Muraja'ah rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 15. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Weak links
points: Where do you pause or swap ayat?
Recite the two ayat around it 5 times

keywords.def: revision of what is already memorised
the older memorised portion, revised on a rota
a place where you often pause or swap ayat

questions.q: Fix the weak link: recite 80:5 to 6 and 80:9 to 10 and say what comes after each فَأَنتَ.
questions.a: 80:6 فَأَنتَ لَهُۥ تَصَدَّىٰ; 80:10 فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ.

questions.q: Best time to fix a weak link?
Breakout pairs: recite your manzil surahs for today to a partner who marks the rubric on the pupil PDF. Today's rota group recites 80:1 to 16 to the teacher.
questions.a: Rubric scores and one target for each partner; the teacher records the rota group's scores.

questions.q: Extend: list your three weakest links in Juz' 'Amma.
Stretch: explain how the meaning helps fix a weak link, with an example.
questions.a: In 80:6 the rich man gets attention; in 80:10 the sincere seeker is neglected: meaning orders the words.
A) فَأَنتَ. Both begin فَأَنتَ (80:6 تَصَدَّىٰ; 80:10 تَلَهَّىٰ): a classic weak link.

questions.q: Think again: Why do people forget surahs they once knew perfectly? What would stop that happening to you?
questions.a: Lack of revision. A steady rota (sabaq, sabqi, manzil) keeps everything fresh.
